newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan students fight riot police, defy president.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan students fight riot police, defy president.

text.p: Thousands of Kenyan students fought riot police in the heart of Nairobi on Monday, defying President Daniel arap Moi a week after the worst political unrest in Kenya in seven years.

The Kenya Polytechnic students seized control for hours of Haile Selassie Avenue, a major highway through the city centre, throwing stones and demanding constitutional reforms before parliamentary and presidential elections later this year.
In another development, Moslem preacher Sheikh Balala, a fierce critic of the president, returned to his home city of Mombasa two years after being forced into exile, witnesses said.
Balala returned to Kenya on Saturday after two years exile in Germany vowing to spearhead a campaign for constitutional reforms
"I don't recognise the forthcoming elections and I would rather voters burned their registration cards," Balala told a crowd of around 1,000 at the Sakina Mosque in the Indian Ocean port.
Nine people were killed in Nairobi and other towns and cities a week ago during fierce clashes between demonstrators and riot police.
Opposition-backed groups have campaigned since April for constitutional reforms that would reduce Moi's power before presidential and parliamentary elections this year. No date is set for the polls.
"Moi must go, Moi must go," chanted the Polytechnic students on Monday. "The time for change is now. We want reforms now," they said.
Witnesses said two people, who were apparently passersby, were seriously injured in the Nairobi clashes. There were no police casualties.

Riot and crack General Service Unit (GSU) police fired teargas and rubber bullets to drive the students back into the polytechnic campus after they hit police and cars with rocks and used slingshots to send stones flying across the wide avenue.
Hundreds of police later stormed the campus and retook the highway. Several women students were beaten during the police charge on campus.
Fourteen people were arrested and would be charged on Tuesday, police said.

Moi, 73 and in power for the last 19 years, said last Friday he would take action against any attempt to bring chaos to the country and challenged the opposition to take the debate on reforms to parliament, where his ruling party has a majority.
Authorities ordered Nairobi University and Jomo Kenyatta University closed indefinitely last week following days of clashes with riot police in the capital.
In addition to the reform issue, students are angered by a draft parliamentary bill requiring the expulsion of those who fail to pay fees. The bill is a World Bank condition for aid.
Anglican Archbishop David Gitari on Sunday verbally attacked Moi from the pulpit at Nairobi's All Saints Cathedral at a ceremonial "cleansing" and re-dedication after riots last week.
Police threw teargas into the cathedral and beat opposition and reform leaders when people fleeing a confrontation between demonstrators and police sought refuge there last Monday.
